Appropriates $200 million for the CEC to create the Demand Side Grid Support Program which incentivizes “dispatchable customer load reduction and backup generation operation as on-call emergency supply and load reduction during extreme events.” SB846 (Dodd, Chapter 239, Statutes of 2022). Directs the CEC to consult with the CPUC and CAISO to set a statewide goal for load shifting to reduce net peak electrical demand and to adjust that target in each biennial integrated energy policy report thereafter. With required consultation with LBNL’s Phase 3 Report, the initial target was set in March 2023 as 7,000 MW of reduced net peak electrical demand of by 2030. SB846 Load Shift Goal Report identifies 3 categories of load flexibility resources, with different goals and levels of departure from the 2022 estimated baseline for each: 1. Load-modifying (e.g., hourly dynamic rates): 3,000 MW ○ 2022 baseline: 657-1,037 MW 2. Resource planning and procurement (i.e., supply side Demand Response): 2,825 MW ○ 2022 baseline: 1,620-1,775 MW 3. Incremental and emergency (i.e., extreme event Demand Response): 1,175 MW ○ 2022 baseline: 1,175 MW 69 California Energy August 2021 introduction of the pilot Market Informed Demand Automation Commission (CEC) Server (MIDAS). Requires that large IOUs, POUs, and CCAs: 1. Maintain the accuracy of existing and future time-varying rates in MIDAS; 2. Develop a standard rate information access tool to support third-party services; 3. Develop and submit locational rates that change at least hourly to reflect marginal wholesale costs; and 4. Integrate information about new time-varying rates and automation technologies into existing customer education and outreach programs Flexible Demand Appliance Standards (called for in SB 49). Devices covered: 1. Pool pumps (final approved regulation February 2024) 2. Requests for Information released in Fall 2024 for low-voltage thermostats and electric vehicle supply equipment 3. Pre-rulemaking language singled out compact and standard electric clothes dryers; compact and standard dishwashers; and low-voltage system thermostats Electric Program Investment Charge (EPIC) R&D support for load flexibility and dynamic prices. In particular, in September 2020, the EPIC program released a competitive solicitation for a flexible load R&D hub. The solicitation required bidders to “develop new demand flexibility technologies consistent with California’s building energy efficiency, appliance, and load management standards … [with] research projects … compatible with … the data resulting from the load management standards” and using MIDAS for “automation signaling.” LBNL was awarded this hub.
